analysis:
Examined threat-model doc changes (new A-018, TB-012, T-059 and header note), plus the new AddonHold.swift value types and the AddonHoldControl.swift request type (only the patch excerpt was supplied, and it was truncated).

AddonHold.swift (lines 1-138) holds only state: hold records with a lease range of 30...600 s, a hold book with one active hold per add-on, and a bounded ended list (32 entries). It has no I/O, authentication or authorization logic. The lease arithmetic `sinceMs + Int64(leaseSeconds) * 1_000` (lines 33, 40) can overflow only if leaseSeconds is unchecked. The bounds are declared at line 9 but enforced elsewhere. The enforcement is not in the supplied evidence, in AddonIPCServer or ProviderLoop+AddonHold. A restored persisted record (the Codable init at line 90) is not range-validated here either. That is a same-UID file, which T-059 declares out of scope.

AddonHoldControl.swift: the request is bound to the target ProcessIdentity and a UUID id, with a 60 s freshness window, a 5 s skew allowance, and lease range checks on hold. The patch was cut off at the status/release case, so I could not verify the rest of isValid or the mailbox authentication.

Threat model: T-059 and TB-012 honestly mark same-UID tampering and coordinator handling of the busy fields as out of scope or accepted. I found no weakening of existing controls and no contradiction with TB-002, TB-003 or the App Attest boundaries (TB-011).

Remaining integration questions for the next pass:
- AddonPeerPolicy audit-token verification.
- AddonIPCServer framing, connection and idle bounds.
- ProviderLoop+AddonHold drain ordering.
- Whether lease and field validation is enforced before AddonHold construction or decode.
- The machine-lock fallback.
- How a hold affects A-018 heartbeat busy fields without exposing consumer data (A-001).
- Whether the operator mailbox is the same-UID lifecycle mailbox with the same trust assumptions.
Those files were not supplied, so no conclusion is drawn about them.
